short: Pitch and energy predicted from lips, face and emotion (M06) is standard: Faces-to-Voices did it in 2025. Prosody metrics improve, WER does not; normalization change unablated.
position: LipSody [@lee2026lipsody] changes the decoder (M06): pitch and energy predicted from lip content, face identity and a face-video emotion embedding condition a LipVoicer-style diffusion model [@yemini2024lipvoicer]. Within video-to-speech the design is standard, not new: 8 earlier studies name a pitch, energy or prosody predictor (pattern match, Appendix), and Faces-to-Voices already predicts pitch and energy from facial expressions next to lips and face identity [@kim2025faces]; the paper cites neither it nor ImaginTalk [@ye2025shushing]. The prosody gain over the reimplemented baseline holds on the paper's own metrics (global F0 deviation 28.87 to 25.15, Table 2), while WER stays at 22.5% against 22.1% (Table 1). The strongest confound is the switch to speaker-wise waveform normalization (§3.2), which changes the energy targets: the baseline keeps LipVoicer's default training settings (§4.2) and no normalization-only control exists; removing the emotion embedding keeps 93% of the energy-consistency gain (Table 4), so that gain comes from the predictors, the normalization or both (inference). The evaluation (M12) is standard, but the claim of state-of-the-art intelligibility (§1) rests on LipVoicer alone, one ASR scorer and no repeated runs (§4.3).
